study: Bottge et al. (2014), Enhanced Anchored Instruction (EAI) blended math, special-ed resource rooms, Exceptional Children
eval_evidence: Conducted/authored by the EAI developers (Bottge et al.; IES grant H324A090179). No independent third-party evaluator; the program's research team ran the RCT.
developer_evidence: The PD workshop was delivered by an experienced practitioner, not the research team: 'a 2-day summer workshop conducted by a middle school math teacher who had taught with EAI for several years.'
cascade_evidence: One transmission hop: the developers' approach was delivered to study teachers by an experienced EAI middle-school teacher (an intermediary trainer), not by developer/research-team trainers directly.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison was explicit Business-As-Usual ('BAU = business as usual'); BAU teachers taught their regular special-ed math (e.g., Calendar Math, NCTM-aligned). No alternative PD/program assigned to control.
coaching_evidence: PD was a 2-day summer workshop plus detailed daily lesson plans; teacher modeling occurred at the workshop. Classroom observers were for fidelity measurement only. No ongoing in-class coaching of teachers reported.
student_dose_evidence: EAI is curriculum taught by the teacher during the regular resource-room math block (explicit instruction + video-anchored problems + hands-on projects); no separate tutoring/pull-out or independent student software dose added beyond instruction.
maturity_evidence: Single 18-week implementation measured immediately post; program is a single-semester design with no second-year/teacher-experience maturity axis described.
